title: Leaf stitch
subtitle: Open diagonal stitches that form a veined, skeletal leaf shape
excerpt: Leaf stitch fills a leaf outline with pairs of long diagonal stitches that cross at the centre spine, leaving an open area down the middle. The result suggests veins rather than solid coverage, giving a light, airy leaf shape.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), leaf stitch entry.

content.text: Leaf stitch is worked from the base of a leaf shape toward the tip, with alternating stitches from the left and right edges. Each stitch travels diagonally to cross the centre spine and ends part way up the opposite side, not at the edge. Because the stitches do not meet edge to edge, the centre of the leaf is open and a vein-like pattern forms at the spine.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands; a single colour reads cleanly

content.text: Transfer the leaf outline and draw a light centre spine from tip to base. Secure the thread on the back.

Bring the needle up at A on the left outer edge near the base. Insert at B on the right side of the centre spine, about halfway up the leaf. The stitch crosses the spine but ends inside the leaf outline, not at the right edge.
Bring the needle up at C on the right outer edge, level with A. Insert at D on the left side of the centre spine, at the same height as B. This mirrors the first stitch.

Continue working alternating left and right stitches, stepping up the leaf toward the tip. Each stitch starts at the outer edge and ends near the spine on the opposite side. The open area in the middle narrows naturally as the leaf tapers.
At the very tip, make one or two small straight stitches to close the point. Secure the thread on the back.

items.symptom: The open centre closes up and the leaf looks solid
items.cause: Each stitch was taken all the way to the opposite edge instead of ending near the spine.
items.fix: End each stitch about one third of the way past the spine, not at the far edge. The open channel down the centre is the defining feature of leaf stitch.

items.symptom: The stitches splay at different angles
items.cause: The start points on each edge are not evenly spaced.
items.fix: Mark equal-interval dots along both edges of the leaf before starting. Matching pairs of dots keep the diagonal angles consistent.

content.text: Leaf stitch is used for open, veined leaves in Jacobean crewel work and floral surface embroidery. For a fully solid leaf fill see
worked in a column down the spine of a leaf gives a similar veined look with less coverage.
